tags.notes: Volcanic islet (former HMS Diamond Rock, 1804); a dozen dive circuits from 0-60m depending on route; a fault/tunnel crosses the islet (the 'cathedral'); depth corrected from 40m to 60m (max depth reported across sources)
The triangular fault/tunnel ('the cathedral') that crosses the Diamond Rock islet; entrance from roughly 16-25m; depth corrected from 20m to 25m

Shallow scree 0-7m with a grassy area where green turtles graze on Thalassia testudinum seagrass; a drop-off beyond the cove reaches ~25m with regular hawksbill turtle sightings; depth corrected from 12m to 25m (max reported); most diving is in the shallow beginner-friendly zone

Fifteen merchant vessels sank in Saint-Pierre's harbor on 8 May 1902; roughly a dozen wrecks are diveable today between about 12m and 60m recreational limits. The deepest known wreck, the Tamaya, lies at 85m and is beyond recreational/closed to diving. Site count corrected from 'at least eight' to fifteen sunk / about a dozen diveable, sourced to Wikipedia's wreck-by-wreck inventory
Black volcanic sand cove connected to Anse Dufour by a short coastal footpath; shares the same resident turtle population

Succession of small canyons and a drop-off north of Case-Pilote; site_type corrected from 'reef' to 'wall' since sources consistently describe the primary feature as a tombant/drop-off with canyons, not a coral reef; depth corrected from 22m to 25m max

Basaltic dome/drop-off between Grande Anse and Anse du Bourg formed by a lava flow; fissures and rockslides descend to 55-60m. A small 3-12m plateau is used for beginners, but the site as a whole is an advanced drop-off dive. Corrected from site_type=reef/depth=12m/difficulty=Beginner based on 3 independent dive-shop sources

Originally the beacon-tender Quinette de Richemond/Rochemont, launched 1911 at Royan for Phares et Balises de Gironde; renamed Masoala (1948) then Caraibe (1957); ran aground at Pointe-a-Pitre in 1966 after Hurricane Ines; rebuilt as a three-masted vessel and renamed Nahoon by Henry Wakelam; deliberately sunk as an artificial reef by local dive centres and the Regional Tourism Committee. Sources disagree on the sinking year (1993 per alphaplongee.com and tribloo.com vs 1994 per espaceplongee-martinique.com) and on length (35m per espaceplongee-martinique.com vs 41m reported elsewhere) - both flagged as unresolved conflicts rather than picked

Between Anse Belleville and Les Abymes, off Le Precheur. Coral plateau from 6-30m leading to a drop-off/gouffre reaching 60m; minimum certification is Niveau 1/Open Water. tags.notes: RE-AUDITED 2026-08-12: cross-checked against en.wikipedia.org 'Wrecks of Saint-Pierre harbor' - vessel name, 1883 build at Aitken & Mansel (Glasgow), 2,712 gross tons, 8 May 1902 sinking, 68 aboard/11 survivors all confirmed, no corrections needed. tags.name: Épave Amelie
tags.notes: RE-AUDITED 2026-08-12: three-masted steel sailing ship (sister to the Belem), built 1890 at the Sevestre shipyard in Chantenay, 48m long, developed a hull leak in Saint-Pierre harbor, towed by the steamer Diamant to Anse Turin for repairs where she sank; the Mont Pelee eruption of 8 May 1902 followed. Depth conflict flagged: sources report 5-8m (snorkeling-report.com), ~12m (Wikipedia), and 4-10m (bellemartinique.com) - depth field set to 12m as the upper bound but the range is noted in the markdown rather than picking one number
